conditions.seoTitle: Hair Loss Conditions We Treat | Nina Ross
conditions.description: Eighteen conditions, from CCCA and traction alopecia to telogen effluvium and scalp folliculitis. Find yours, then find out what's actually driving it.
conditions.lede: Find what matches what you have been seeing, then find out what is actually driving it. Serving all of Metro Atlanta.

hero.alt: A scalp seen up close under magnification, showing follicles and fine flaking between hairs.
hero.caption: What the mirror misses, at 200x.

short.text: We specialize in 18 hair loss conditions across six families: scarring, autoimmune, hormonal, inflammatory, traumatic and other systemic causes. The family matters because it changes what's possible. Scarring conditions need early action to protect follicles that are still alive. In others, including alopecia areata and anagen effluvium, the follicle usually survives. A 200x read of your scalp, alongside a look at the systems behind it, is how we tell which one you have.
takeaways: Scarred follicles do not regrow, so early matters most there.
One visit tells us which family you're in.

families.name: Scarring
families.title: Scarring conditions
families.text: Inflammation replaces the follicle with scar tissue. Early reading protects what is still alive.
families.callout: Scarred follicles do not regrow. The goal of catching it early is protecting every follicle that is still active.

items.name: CCCA
items.text: Central centrifugal cicatricial alopecia. Starts at the crown and spreads outward, quietly.

items.name: Lichen Planopilaris
items.text: An inflammatory scarring alopecia that often burns or stings before it shows.

families.name: Autoimmune
families.title: Autoimmune conditions
families.text: The immune system interrupts the follicle. The follicle itself often survives.

items.name: Alopecia Areata
items.text: Smooth, round patches that appear quickly. The follicle usually survives.

items.name: Lichen Planus
items.text: An immune condition of skin, nails and mouth that can reach the follicle.

families.name: Hormonal
families.title: Hormonal conditions
families.text: Estrogen, thyroid, DHT and cortisol shifts show up as thinning through the top.

items.name: Hormonal Hair Loss
items.text: Four hormones do most of the work. When they move, your hair reports it.

items.name: PCOS Hair Loss
items.text: Higher androgens thin the crown and thicken hair where you did not ask for it.

items.name: Excess DHT
items.text: The hormone behind pattern thinning, and how to tell if it is your driver.

items.name: Female Hair Loss
items.text: The widening part and the thinner ponytail, explained honestly.

items.name: Male Pattern Baldness
items.text: Predictable pattern, variable speed. The earlier you read it, the more you keep.

items.name: Postpartum Hair Loss
items.text: The shedding that starts around month three. It is real, and it does end.

families.name: Inflammatory
families.title: Inflammatory conditions
families.text: Bumps, scale and irritation that keep the scalp inflamed and the density falling.

items.name: Scalp Folliculitis
items.text: Tender, sometimes pus-filled bumps sitting right on the follicle.

items.name: Seborrheic Dermatitis
items.text: Greasy flaking and itch that keep the scalp inflamed.

items.name: Scalp Bumps
items.text: Start here if you are feeling bumps and do not know what they are.

families.name: Traumatic
families.title: Traumatic conditions
families.text: Tension, pulling or treatment interrupts follicles that were otherwise healthy.

items.name: Traction Alopecia
items.text: Tension-driven loss at the edges and part lines. Often reversible early.

items.name: Trichotillomania
items.text: We treat the scalp. No judgment, no behavioral advice.

items.name: Anagen Effluvium
items.text: Rapid loss during treatment. The follicles usually survive.

families.name: Other
families.title: Other conditions
families.text: Systemic drivers that show up as shedding across the whole scalp.

items.name: Telogen Effluvium
items.text: Sudden diffuse shedding, usually about three months after a trigger.

items.name: Medication Hair Loss
items.text: Which medications are associated with shedding, and the right next step.

treatments.description: Eight treatments, from PRP and exosomes to red light and IV nutrients. Which one is right depends entirely on what your scalp and your systems show.
treatments.lede: One rule: treatment selection follows diagnosis. Here's what each treatment does, and what it's often considered for. Serving all of Metro Atlanta.

hero.alt: Follicles seen at 200x magnification during a scalp read.
hero.caption: Every plan starts with a 200x read.

short.text: We offer eight treatments, from PRP and exosomes to red light and IV nutrients, and which one is right depends entirely on what your scalp and your systems show. That's why treatment selection follows diagnosis, and diagnosis starts with the $99 Hair & Body Discovery. Every hands-on treatment is performed by a certified trichologist, with protocols overseen by Dr. Nina Ross, ND, as Clinical Director.
takeaways: Diagnosis comes first, then the treatment.
Most plans combine more than one.
Every treatment is done in-house by certified trichologists.

families.name: The program
families.title: The flagship program
families.text: Ten visits that bring several treatments together, sequenced around what your scalp shows and adjusted as you progress.

items.name: Restorative Therapy
items.text: Growth factors, microneedling, red and blue lasers, LED infrared and targeted supplementation across ten visits, built around what your scalp showed us.

families.name: Regenerative
families.title: Regenerative treatments
families.text: Treatments that work on follicles that are still viable, which is why we screen before we recommend any of them.

items.name: PRP Therapy
items.text: Platelet-rich plasma for follicles that are still viable. We screen candidates first.

items.name: Exosome Therapy
items.text: Growth signals delivered straight to the follicle, and how we decide whether it fits your case.

items.name: Growth Factors Therapy
items.text: Concentrated growth signals applied to the scalp to support follicles that are still active.

items.name: Microneedling
items.text: Controlled micro-injury that triggers repair and helps topicals absorb.

families.name: Nutrient delivery
families.title: Nutrient delivery
families.text: For when the labs show a gap that oral supplements haven't closed.

items.name: IV Nutrient Therapy
items.text: When absorption is the limiting factor and oral supplements stall.

items.name: Fusion Mesotherapy
items.text: Micro-injections that deliver nutrients into the scalp where follicles can use them.

families.name: Light therapy
families.title: Light therapy
families.text: Low-level light used on its own or inside a wider plan, to support the scalp while other care does its work.

items.name: Red Light Therapy
items.text: Low-level light that supports follicle activity and calms inflammation.
